entries.title: Genetic Terminology (Penetrance, Expressivity, Heterogeneity, Mosaicism)

testable_competencies.vocabulary: Recognize the definitions of penetrance, expressivity, genetic/allelic/locus/phenotypic heterogeneity, and mosaicism as background for interpreting the inheritance patterns and conditions covered later in the chapter.

entries.zero_question_reason: Pure terminology glossary; not itself an independently testable clinical competency, and not a named MCC objective topic - it frames the disease- and inheritance-pattern-specific units that follow.

entries.title: Non-Mendelian Inheritance Patterns (Triplet Repeat Expansion/Anticipation, Imprinting/Uniparental Disomy, Mitochondrial Inheritance)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's causal_conditions explicitly names 'Non-Mendelian (e.g., mitochondrial, epigenetic)' inheritance as a category the candidate must recognize; triplet-repeat anticipation and imprinting/uniparental disomy are the mechanisms underlying this category, though not individually named.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize triplet-repeat anticipation, genomic imprinting/uniparental disomy, and mitochondrial (maternal) inheritance as distinct non-Mendelian inheritance mechanisms, with awareness of their prototypical example conditions (e.g., Fragile X, Huntington disease, Prader-Willi/Angelman syndromes).

do_not_test: Molecular mechanism detail beyond the pattern-recognition level (e.g., specific methylation biochemistry, exact repeat-length cutoffs) - specialist genomic minutiae without direct MCC objective support.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's enabling_objectives explicitly lists 'a family tree' among the clinical findings the candidate must list and interpret for a patient with suspected genetic etiology.

testable_competencies.interpretation: Construct and interpret a three-generation pedigree, including standard symbols and inheritance-pattern recognition (autosomal dominant/recessive, X-linked).
testable_competencies.communication: Affirm a gender-diverse patient's gender identity while separately clarifying sex assigned at birth/chromosomal sex where genetically relevant to pedigree construction.

entries.title: Genetic Testing and Counselling

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's enabling_objectives explicitly requires the candidate to construct a management plan including 'referral for genetic counselling', 'examination of reproductive options', and 'referral for specialized evaluation, genetic testing, community resources, and social and psychological support services.'

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Communicator - Accurately convey relevant information and explanations to patients, families, and communities
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Group's enabling text: 'Adhere to requirements for obtaining informed consent' and 'Respect patients' rights to be given complete and truthful information' - applies generically to the informed-consent and result-disclosure aspects of genetic testing, though genetic counselling is not separately named.

testable_competencies.counselling: Identify indications for presymptomatic testing, newborn screening, preconception counselling, and preimplantation genetic diagnosis, and construct an initial management plan including referral for genetic counselling and testing.
testable_competencies.consent: Apply informed-consent principles when discussing genetic testing options, including the implications of a positive result for the patient and family members.

do_not_test: Table 1's technical assay-comparison detail (karyotype vs. FISH vs. microarray vs. Sanger vs. NGS vs. MLPA vs. PCR mechanics) beyond recognizing which broad test category is indicated for a given clinical scenario - specialist laboratory-genomics minutiae without direct MCC objective support.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36-2's rationale and title directly name congenital anomalies and dysmorphic features as the objective's core scope; this unit's minor/major-anomaly and malformation/disruption/deformation/dysplasia classification is the foundational framework the objective's key/enabling objectives build on.

testable_competencies.classification: Differentiate minor vs. major anomalies and classify an anomaly's mechanism (malformation, disruption, deformation, dysplasia), and distinguish an association from a sequence and a syndrome (e.g., VACTERL association, Potter sequence, CHARGE syndrome).

entries.title: Approach to the Patient with Physical Differences (Dysmorphology Assessment)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36-2's enabling_objectives explicitly requires a complete history with attention to teratogenic exposures and family history, and a physical exam attentive to 'recognizable phenotypic patterns (e.g., trisomy 21 syndrome)' - directly matching this unit's structured history and dysmorphology physical-exam approach.

testable_competencies.history: Elicit a three-generation family pedigree and prenatal/teratogenic exposure history in a patient with suspected congenital anomalies or dysmorphic features.
testable_competencies.examination: Perform a systematic dysmorphology physical examination (craniofacial, ocular, otic, spinal, limb features) and compare findings against family members.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Text explicitly cross-references Obstetrics (OB4, prenatal/teratogenic exposure history) and Pediatrics (P26, developmental history); overlap to be reconciled once OB and P chapters are mapped.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's causal_conditions explicitly names 'Chromosomal (e.g., aneuploidy, rearrangements)' as a core category the candidate must diagnose.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36-2's causal_conditions cites 'trisomy 21, fragile X syndrome' as the named genetic-disorder example, and its enabling objectives cite 'recognizable phenotypic patterns (e.g., trisomy 21 syndrome)' as a specific physical-exam target.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the characteristic phenotype, associated cardiac/GI/other anomalies, and prognosis of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), and relate incidence to advanced maternal age.

entries.title: Sex Chromosome Disorders and Fragile X Syndrome (Turner Syndrome, Klinefelter Syndrome, Fragile X Syndrome)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's causal_conditions names 'Chromosomal (e.g., aneuploidy, rearrangements)'; Turner (45,X) and Klinefelter (47,XXY) are sex-chromosome aneuploidies, and Fragile X is the objective's implicit trinucleotide-repeat/monogenic category.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36-2's causal_conditions names 'fragile X syndrome' directly; Turner and Klinefelter phenotypes fall within the same dysmorphic-features recognition scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the characteristic phenotype and key complications of Turner syndrome (short stature, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea), Klinefelter syndrome (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, infertility), and Fragile X syndrome (intellectual disability, macroorchidism, premutation-related risks).

entries.title: Microdeletion and Other Recognizable Genetic Syndromes (22q11.2/DiGeorge Syndrome, Prader-Willi Syndrome, Angelman Syndrome, Noonan Syndrome, CHARGE Syndrome)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's causal_conditions covers chromosomal and non-Mendelian (imprinting-related) categories broadly; these named syndromes (22q11.2 deletion, Prader-Willi/Angelman via imprinting, Noonan, CHARGE) are instances of that scope but are not individually named in the objective text.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the hallmark phenotype of the most clinically significant named microdeletion/imprinting syndromes (22q11.2 deletion/DiGeorge: conotruncal cardiac defect, hypocalcemia, immunodeficiency; Prader-Willi: hypotonia then hyperphagia/obesity; Angelman: severe intellectual disability with inappropriate happy affect; Noonan: pulmonary stenosis, webbed neck; CHARGE).

entries.title: Familial Cancer Syndromes (Li-Fraumeni, Lynch, FAP, Hereditary Breast/Ovarian Cancer, Von Hippel-Lindau, Cowden, Neurofibromatosis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's causal_conditions lists 'Postnatal environmental influences (e.g., cancer, type 2 diabetes)' under polygenic/multifactorial disorders generically, but does not name monogenic hereditary cancer syndromes specifically; no MCC objective is titled for hereditary cancer predisposition.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the gene and associated cancer pattern for the most clinically significant hereditary cancer syndromes (e.g., BRCA1/2-Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer, MSH2/MLH1-Lynch syndrome, APC-FAP, TP53-Li-Fraumeni) as a trigger for genetics referral and enhanced surveillance.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Gynecology (BRCA/hereditary breast-ovarian cancer, already completed - GY's crosswalk should be checked for an existing overlapping unit) and General/Thoracic Surgery and Gastroenterology (colorectal-cancer syndromes, both already completed). To be reconciled during the global cross-chapter overlap audit.

entries.title: Cross-Referenced Single-Gene Disorders (Sickle Cell Disease, Cystic Fibrosis)
entries.zero_question_reason: Both entries are pure cross-references with zero independent MG-chapter content ('see Hematology, H21' for Sickle Cell Disease; 'More information found in other chapters' for Cystic Fibrosis); substantive coverage is owned by chapter H (completed) and the relevant Cystic Fibrosis-owning chapter.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Sickle Cell Disease is already covered in chapter H (Hematology). Cystic Fibrosis ownership to be confirmed once the relevant chapter (Respirology or Pediatrics) is mapped.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's 'Monogenic (single gene mutations)' causal_conditions category covers Wilson disease's ATP7B etiology generically, but no MCC objective is titled for Wilson disease or copper-metabolism disorders specifically.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize Wilson disease presenting with liver disease, movement disorder, and/or Kayser-Fleischer rings in a young patient, and initiate chelation therapy referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's 'Monogenic (single gene mutations)' causal_conditions category covers DMD's dystrophin-gene etiology generically, but no MCC objective is titled for muscular dystrophy specifically.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize Duchenne muscular dystrophy presenting with proximal muscle weakness, positive Gowers' sign, and calf pseudohypertrophy in a young boy, and identify creatine kinase elevation and molecular testing as the diagnostic approach.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36's enabling_objectives explicitly names Tay-Sachs disease as its own worked example: 'The candidate will recognize where disease in a patient might reflect the existence of risk factors inherent to a given population (e.g., Tay-Sachs disease).'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize Tay-Sachs disease presenting in infancy with progressive neurodegeneration and a cherry-red macular spot, and identify population-based carrier-risk factors (e.g., Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry) relevant to preconception/prenatal counselling.

entries.title: Metabolic Diseases (Inborn Errors of Metabolism: General Approach, Newborn Screening, Acute Presentation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Inborn errors of metabolism are inherited (mostly autosomal recessive) conditions squarely within objective 36's 'Monogenic (single gene mutations)' causal_conditions category, and the unit's core competency (recognizing at-risk infants and initiating urgent workup) matches the objective's construct-a-management-plan enabling text.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74-1's enabling_objectives explicitly names 'discussing newborn metabolic screening with caregivers' as part of the routine newborn assessment management plan.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize infants and children presenting with failure to thrive, developmental delay, or acute metabolic decompensation as possibly reflecting an inborn error of metabolism, and understand the role of universal newborn screening in early detection.
testable_competencies.initial_management: Identify the initial investigations for a child with suspected acute metabolic decompensation (electrolytes/anion gap, blood glucose, lactate/ammonia, urine studies) and the principle of discontinuing feeds pending workup.

do_not_test: Table 8's exhaustive list of individually named metabolic disorders and their specific enzyme deficiencies/biochemical pathways beyond a recognition-level approach - specialist biochemical-genetics minutiae without direct MCC objective support.

entries.title: Landmark Medical Genetics Trials
do_not_test: Landmark trial names/details/historical trivia - explicitly listed in task instructions as a do-not-test example, consistent with the Landmark-Trials treatment in chapters A, C, CP, D, E, FM, GM, G.
entries.zero_question_reason: Bibliographic/trial-reference material; relevant evidence-based practice points (e.g., PKU dietary management) are already reflected within the disease units' own management competencies.
